raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Raise the package minimum to CuTeDSL 4.7.1 and the optional JAX dependency group to JAX 0.6.0. This makes installation enforce the supported baseline without adding version-dependent test logic.

## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran pre-commit on the changed files and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the applicable AGENTS.md rules. Rule 7 now documents the new package floor; existing runtime gates remain intact.
- [ ] Required labels: `cat-routine-update`, `area:packaging`, `orig-nv-eng` (plus `mod-cutedsl`). GitHub denied the author's label update; a maintainer needs to apply them.

## Affected area

Build, packaging, and installation.

## Summary

- Require `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]>=4.7.1`, preserving the Windows ARM64 exclusion.
- Require `jax>=0.6.0` in the JAX dependency group and align the JAX diagnostic and documentation.
- Update the three Docker recipes that explicitly install an older CuTeDSL, and align package-floor guidance.

## Why

[CuTeDSL 4.7.1 declares its minimum supported JAX version as 0.6.0](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/blob/v4.7.1/python/CuTeDSL/cutlass/jax/__init__.py). Enforce these minimums through dependency metadata.

## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

Installations pinned below CuTeDSL 4.7.1 must upgrade, including downstream environments that still pin 4.6.2. JAX remains opt-in. Kernel-specific runtime gates and BSA's stronger JAX requirement are unchanged. No test code or version-dependent skips are added.

## Testing

- `uv pip compile pyproject.toml --group jax --python-platform x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --python-version 3.11 --resolution lowest-direct --no-build --no-header --no-annotate` — passed; resolved CuTeDSL 4.7.1 and JAX/JAXlib 0.6.0 with their dependencies.
- `uvx pre-commit run --files <changed files>` — passed.
- GPU suites and Docker image builds were not run on the local macOS host; this change updates dependency metadata, installation recipes, documentation, and diagnostic text.

* **Documentation**
  * Updated installation guidance and compatibility requirements to specify CuTeDSL 4.7.1 or later and JAX 0.6.0 or later.
  * Clarified that supported test runs use compatible versions, replacing guidance to skip tests on older DSL versions.
* **Chores**
  * Updated benchmark and test container images to use CuTeDSL 4.7.1.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `9146116c396c` against base `84eadd2074fa`.

The dependency-floor alignment makes sense; I found no approval-blocking regression in this diff. Current vLLM 0.32.0 and SGLang 0.5.22 already pin CuTeDSL 4.8.0, so the historical 4.6.2 pin is not a conflict with those releases (older pinned environments still need an upgrade). Please coordinate the CI pins and consider the minimum-JAX import fix below before landing.

**[P2] Include the helper dependency needed by the advertised minimum JAX stack** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/9146116c396cb89b798eacc3386eb48ba06d6a37/pyproject.toml#L123))

With JAX/jaxlib 0.6.0 and CuTeDSL 4.7.1, dependency resolution succeeds but `import cutlass` fails: `cutlass.jax.ffi -> jax.export -> jax._src.export._export -> from absl import logging`, raising `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'absl'`. Neither the resolved dependency graph nor JAX 0.6.0's metadata supplies absl-py. Adding only absl-py makes the exact-head FE JAX import and CPU metadata helpers pass. Please include the needed helper in the JAX group (or choose a verified minimum that supplies it), and add a small minimum-version import smoke check. This is an existing allowed-stack packaging gap surfaced by validating the new documented minimum, not a newly introduced kernel regression. The current bridge test module skips JAX below 0.9.1, so that suite cannot check this minimum.

Evidence: Lowest-direct dependency resolution omitted absl-py; isolated Python 3.12/JAX 0.6.0/CuTeDSL 4.7.1 import failed before installing absl-py and passed after installing only that helper. Exact PR Python source import was asserted. Attribution: Pre-existing allowed-version dependency gap, directly relevant to this PR's minimum-version contract.

**[P2] Coordinate the CI dependency pins with the new package floor** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/9146116c396cb89b798eacc3386eb48ba06d6a37/pyproject.toml#L53))

The current OSS CI installation still has exact CuTeDSL 4.6.2 and 4.7.0 selections and resolves that exact requirement together with the frontend wheel. Both conflict with the new >=4.7.1 requirement, so those lanes will fail installation before reaching tests. Please land the corresponding CI pin update before running these lanes or merging the new floor. I reproduced the unsatisfiable 4.6.2/new-floor combination with the resolver; I have not started GPU jobs that would stop at this known installation conflict.

Evidence: Read the current CI installation constraints and confirmed an isolated resolver failure for nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2 alongside this PR's pyproject.toml. Attribution: Required CI companion update for the intentional dependency-floor change.

- **[P2] Still open:** [Align the remaining KDA JAX installation guidance](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1819#discussion_r4364341632).

Validation: Read all 19 changed files; executable Python changes are diagnostics, with no kernel or numerical changes. Deterministic precheck produced no candidates. Linux x86-64 lowest-direct dependency resolution succeeds with CuTeDSL 4.7.1 and JAX/jaxlib 0.6.0; a separate exact-4.6.2 constraint fails resolution as expected. Python 3.12 CPU smoke check asserts exact PR Python imports, lazy base cudnn import, JAX 0.6.0/CuTeDSL 4.7.1 bridge availability, zeros_init, and operand/scale-factor metadata helpers. RED without absl-py; GREEN after adding only absl-py. Verified current published downstream dependency metadata for vLLM 0.32.0 and SGLang 0.5.22. This is a packaging compatibility check, not a downstream execution test. Current-head pre-commit, documentation, CodeQL and dependency-review checks pass. PR labels, milestone and project metadata were completed. GPU CI deferred pending the conflicting dependency-pin update.

Limitations: No GPU execution qualification at the minimum JAX version, no fresh FE extension build, and no Docker image rebuild. The smoke check used the exact PR Python source with a compatible prebuilt FE extension. No performance or determinism claim: this diff does not change kernel arithmetic or scheduling.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
